headline: High: TREK’s MCP and secret-bearing collaborative workspace create the main risk; Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can amplify leakage and bad actions if its outputs are trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK exposes MCP and real-time collaboration, so attacker-controlled content can reach its tool layer; Perplexity runs browser-based search and can ingest web content. The pair lacks documented provenance controls between Perplexity outputs and TREK inputs, so prompt injection is plausible in default use, though not proven high because no shared channel is explicit.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Perplexity-generated text into MCP-connected tools without sanitization
IF Perplexity browses attacker-controlled pages that TREK later treats as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic import of Perplexity outputs into TREK tools
Require provenance labels on all web-derived text before MCP use
Use a manual review step for any copied instructions
Restrict TREK MCP endpoints to allowlisted actions only

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and logs in shared files, while Perplexity sends queries and uploaded documents to vendor-hosted inference/search services. If sensitive TREK data is pasted or uploaded into Perplexity, leakage to a third party is immediate and potentially irreversible; the pair’s default collaboration model makes this a dangerous default-path risk.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservation data are copied into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Perplexity retains browsing context containing TREK-sensitive material
mitigations: Block secrets from being pasted into Perplexity
Redact confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets before any query
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Perplexity-assisted planning
Turn off or minimize retention where available
requires-engineering: add DLP filters between TREK exports and external LLM prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and does not write the host filesystem, but TREK is self-hosted, collaborative, and uses files plus MCP. The overlap is mainly on shared mutable planning data and external APIs, not direct same-directory writes, so conflict exists but is narrower than high; uncertainty remains because TREK’s exact locking behavior is undocumented.
conditions: IF TREK instances edit the same travel.db or uploads concurrently
IF Perplexity-derived edits are applied to TREK without coordination
mitigations: Use one writer per TREK workspace at a time
Lock shared records before applying edits
Review diffs before saving itinerary changes
Separate read-only research from write-capable planning sessions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a citation-heavy answer engine, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in; if TREK treats Perplexity’s output as authoritative, bad travel facts can cascade into reservations, budgets, or itinerary changes. The pair has no documented verification gate, so the default path can propagate errors into downstream actions.
conditions: IF TREK uses Perplexity output as a source of truth without human verification
IF itinerary or reservation actions are triggered from copied Perplexity answers
mitigations: Require human verification before booking or editing reservations
Cross-check dates, prices, and locations against primary sources
Mark Perplexity output as untrusted until reviewed
Use TREK approval gates for any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles EU-style personal data, reservations, email addresses, and secrets in a self-hosted system, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with vendor-only egress and uploaded-document processing. If regulated travel or identity data flows from TREK into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations can be breached; the pairwise compliance gap is driven by Perplexity’s external processing.
conditions: IF TREK data subject to residency or retention rules is sent to Perplexity
IF uploaded documents contain personal data or booking records
mitigations: Keep regulated personal data out of Perplexity prompts
Use anonymized summaries instead of raw reservations
Document a data-processing boundary for external search
requires-engineering: route sensitive workflows to a compliant local model
